_note: Bulk hypotheses about Lords2.exe: names that are consistent with everything
measured but that no check has yet tried to falsify. They are NOT symbols.
docs/symbols.json is the verified tier and its ratio is deliberately high; a
name only moves there once someone has run a check that could have failed and
it did not. This file exists so that leads can be written down in bulk without
diluting that. Correction C3 in docs/decisions.md is what a coherent, unchecked
model costs when it is filed as fact.
Every entry carries a 'basis': the mechanical observation the guess rests on -
an L2.eng group and index, a widget-table membership, a shipped filename. An
entry whose basis is only 'it is called from near something named' is the shape
correction C3 took and should be treated as a question, not an answer.
'confidence' is the author's own estimate, in the same words the pilot measured:
'subject'  - what the function is about is anchored to a string or an asset;
the role word in the name is the part that may be wrong.
'role'     - the role is anchored (it is in a widget table, it is a painter);
the subject is the guess.
'both'     - neither half has an independent anchor. Read this before using it.
Promote an entry by deleting it from here and adding it to docs/symbols.json
with the check that promoted it written into its comment.
Two further fields, added when a second subsystem started using this file:
'promotion' - the check that would move the entry into symbols.json, named IN
ADVANCE. A criterion invented after the evidence arrives is not a
criterion. "Read it" is a fine one; "it will become clear" is not.
'claims'    - a top-level array for readings that are not about one address: a
field's meaning, an off-by-one, a rule. Those previously had
nowhere to live and went into prose instead.
And a rule this file did not state: an address VERIFIED in docs/symbols.json must
not also appear here. Two subsystems reached g_screenIdSaved from opposite
directions within a day, one filing it as a hypothesis and one as verified. The
verified entry wins and the hypothesis is deleted.

functions.name: Ui_DispatchPointer
functions.basis: 8,140 bytes, the largest unnamed function in the interface. Its opening is Screen_HitRegion, then Screen_HandleInput, then a per-screen fallback chain that on the campaign map tries Map_EdgeScroll, Menu_OpenDropdown(g_menuBarItems, 3), CountyStrip_Click, CountyStrip_JobClick and Map_Click in that order. It writes g_screenId with 30 different values - more than any other function in the binary.
functions.comment: The top-level pointer dispatcher: one click, routed to whatever the current screen wants. Only the first 6% of the body has been read; the name claims the role, not the whole behaviour.

functions.name: SaveLoad_Accept
functions.basis: Record 0 of g_saveLoadWidgets (0x004DDD78), frame 29 at (304, 64) - the tick of the tick/cross pair whose cross is the verified SaveLoad_Cancel. Its whole body is DAT_005CD41C = 100.
functions.comment: The save/load box's confirm button. What the sentinel 100 means to its reader has not been traced.

functions.name: Screen_MapInfo
functions.basis: The painter Screen_Draw dispatches for g_screenId 0x04, which FUN_0042FF10 sets after a map click that picked something. Branches to UnitPanel_Draw when a unit is picked and FUN_0041BEFE otherwise, on the same g_pickedTileFlags bits Map_Click uses.
functions.comment: docs/screens-county.md calls this 'the map information panel'; nothing has read what it draws.

functions.name: Merchant_DrawPanel
functions.basis: The widget-pass companion Screen_DrawWidgets calls for screen 0x08, immediately before Widget_Draw on the merchant's own table.
functions.comment: The merchant screen's per-frame overlay. Subject is anchored by the screen id; what it draws is unread.

functions.name: Merchant_HandleInput
functions.basis: The input-pass companion Screen_HandleInput calls for screen 0x08, before Widget_Test on the merchant's table.
functions.comment: The merchant screen's non-widget hit-testing.

functions.name: Armoury_DrawPanel
functions.basis: Called by Screen_DrawWidgets for both armoury screens, 0x0A and 0x0D.
functions.comment: Shared overlay for the armoury and the armoury's buy list.

functions.name: Armoury_HandleInput
functions.basis: Called by Screen_HandleInput for screens 0x0A and 0x0D, before Hotspot_Test on a 9-entry table at 0x004DC938.
functions.comment: Shared input for the armoury screens.

functions.name: SendSupplies_DrawPanel
functions.basis: Called by Screen_DrawWidgets for screen 0x18, whose painter Screen_SendSupplies draws L2.eng group 33, 'Send supplies'.
functions.comment: The send-supplies overlay.

functions.name: SendSupplies_Close
functions.basis: Records 0 and 1 of the send-supplies widget table 0x004DD538: frames 29 and 31 at (320, 342) and (360, 346), hotspot ids 1 and 0 - the tick/cross convention. It writes g_screenId twice.
functions.comment: Accept or cancel the supply shipment; the hotspot id says which.

functions.name: SendSupplies_Less
functions.basis: Records 2 and 4 of the same table, frame 27 at x 216, hotspot ids 0 and 2 - two rows of a pair whose other half is 0x0043B27A at frame 25.
functions.comment: Decrease the amount of one commodity.

functions.name: SendSupplies_More
functions.basis: Records 3 and 5 of the same table, frame 25 at x 296, hotspot ids 0 and 2.
functions.comment: Increase the amount of one commodity.

functions.name: CastleBuild_Close
functions.basis: Both records of the castle-build widget table 0x004DDB80, frames 29 and 31 at (432, 440) and (472, 444), hotspot ids 1 and 0. It writes g_screenId five times.
functions.comment: Accept or abandon the castle design, on the verified Screen_CastleBuild.

functions.name: Armoury_BuyLess
functions.basis: Record 0 of the armoury buy table 0x004DD8C8, frame 68 at (176, 44); the four buttons in that row are frames 68, 66, 58 and 60, and 68/66 is the minus/plus pair the diplomacy gift row also uses.
functions.comment: One of the armoury buy-list's four buttons; the pairing is the evidence, not the body.

functions.name: Armoury_BuyMore
functions.basis: Record 1 of 0x004DD8C8, frame 66 at (208, 44).
functions.comment: The other half of the minus/plus pair.

functions.name: Armoury_BuyPrev
functions.basis: Record 2 of 0x004DD8C8, frame 58 at (240, 44). Frames 58 and 60 have not been identified in the button sheet.
functions.comment: Unanchored: only its position in the table is known.

functions.name: Armoury_BuyNext
functions.basis: Record 3 of 0x004DD8C8, frame 60 at (272, 44).
functions.comment: Unanchored: only its position in the table is known.

functions.name: SiegePrep_Add
functions.basis: Records 0, 2 and 4 of the siege-preparation widget table 0x004DDF10, frame 21 at x 38 and y 184 / 252 / 320, hotspot ids 0, 1 and 2. Screen_SiegePrep draws L2.eng group 83, whose indices 1, 2 and 3 are Catapults, Siege towers and Battering rams in that order. The body caps the count at 4, 4 and 2 respectively and refuses in a network game.
functions.comment: Order one more siege engine of the row's type. The caps 4 / 4 / 2 are read off the body and are not yet cross-checked against play.

functions.name: SiegePrep_Remove
functions.basis: Records 1, 3 and 5 of 0x004DDF10, frame 23, each 26 pixels below its partner, same hotspot ids. Decrements the same field while it is above zero.
functions.comment: Cancel one ordered siege engine.

functions.name: Diplo_AdjustGift
functions.basis: Records 6 and 7 of g_diploWidgets, frames 68 and 66 at (184, 240) and (216, 240), hotspot ids 1 and 0 - the minus/plus pair. The screen it sits on draws L2.eng group 72 index 18, 'Gift of', beside g_diploGold.
functions.comment: Raise or lower the offered gift; the hotspot id says which way.

functions.name: SmackTest_Step
functions.basis: Records 0 and 1 of the screen 0x44 widget table 0x004DDFA0, frames 68 and 66 at (208, 232) and (240, 232). Screen 0x44's painter draws L2.eng group 89, whose index 0 is 'Smack file testing'.
functions.comment: Pick the previous or next Smacker file on the developers' test screen.

functions.name: SmackTest_Close
functions.basis: Records 2 and 3 of 0x004DDFA0, frames 29 and 31 - the tick/cross pair. It writes g_screenId.
functions.comment: Leave the Smacker test screen.

functions.name: Ratings_DrawPanel
functions.basis: Called by Screen_DrawWidgets for both 0x2E and 0x2F, the two Battle Master screens, and by Menu_NewGame before it opens its confirmation box.
functions.comment: Shared overlay for the two score screens. Being called from Menu_NewGame as well means the role may be wider than 'the ratings panel' - read it before promoting.

functions.name: Net_JournalCommand
functions.comment: Records an executed deterministic command into a ring of 0x38-byte slots at 0x0050D7C0: a live flag, the sub-opcode, and twelve int arguments. Both the writer and the reader of every command opcode call it, so it sees each command exactly once per peer.
functions.basis: Read in full. The slot layout is unambiguous - 0x0050D7C6 flag, 0x0050D7C7 sub-opcode, 0x0050D7C0 + 4*n arguments, stride 0x38. Every command writer/reader pair traced so far ends in a call to it. What is inferred is the PURPOSE: 'journal' rather than 'apply'. Nothing in the function itself changes game state.
functions.promotion: Find the consumer of the 0x0050D7C0 ring. If it replays the slots, this is a journal; if it is only a debug overlay, the name is wrong. Either answer is a check that could fail.

functions.name: NetCmd_ReadMoveOrder
functions.comment: The receiving half of network command 0x29: reads player (1), a 4-byte value, unit (1), x (2), y (2) and journals sub-opcode 0x0C.
functions.basis: It sits between g_netCmdWriters[0x29] and g_netCmdWriters[0x2A] in address order, uses Net_ReadField where its neighbour used Net_WriteField, reads the same five widths in the same order, and passes the same sub-opcode 0x0C to Net_JournalCommand. The writer half IS verified and is in symbols.json.
functions.promotion: The reader is never called from the command table, so its caller has to be found - presumably a dispatch keyed on the received opcode byte. Naming that dispatcher promotes every reader at once.

functions.name: Net_ResolveDest
functions.comment: Turns 0x00544094 into the 4-byte value NetCmd_WriteMoveOrder puts second in the packet, ahead of the unit index.
functions.basis: Position in the payload only. Not read.

functions.name: Move_DistanceAcrossExpensive
functions.comment: Map_HoverUnitTarget uses it instead of the raw distance field whenever that field reads 100 or more, then adds 1. 100 is the cost the cost map gives an impassable-in-practice tile - castle, settlement, dwelling plot - so this looks like 'what would the cost be if the last step onto the objective were free'.
functions.basis: The call site and the 99 threshold, which matches Move_BuildCostMap's 100 exactly. The function body was not read.
functions.promotion: Read it, and check the result against a hand-computed path onto a county town in the England fixture.

functions.name: Unit_AbandonOrders
functions.comment: One of the three callers of Siege_Break, and it passes g_movingUnit.
functions.basis: The Siege_Break call and the argument. Body not read.
functions.promotion: Read it. It is 286 bytes and it is the only unread member of a three-caller set whose other two are verified.

functions.name: Merchant_OpenScreen
functions.comment: Map_Click's branch for clicking a type-3 unit that is the local player's.
functions.basis: Position in Map_Click's dispatch only, against an existing symbols.json comment that says the merchant branch opens screen 0x08. Body not read.
functions.promotion: Read it and check it sets g_screenId to 8.

globals.name: g_fileListTop
globals.basis: The only value SaveLoad_Scroll moves, by the widget's hotspot id, clamped at 0 and against DAT_004EB25C with a window of 15 rows for list 1 and 5 for list 2.
globals.comment: First visible row of the save/load file list.

globals.name: g_fileListCount
globals.basis: The bound SaveLoad_Scroll clamps g_fileListTop against.
globals.comment: How many files the save/load list holds.

globals.name: g_netCmdJournal
globals.comment: Ring of 0x38-byte records Net_JournalCommand fills: +6 live flag, +7 sub-opcode, +0 and +4.. twelve int arguments.
globals.basis: The write pattern in Net_JournalCommand, which is unambiguous about the layout and silent about the purpose.

globals.name: g_netPacketBuf
globals.comment: Forty 0x104-byte outgoing command packets. +0 opcode, +1 declared length, +2 a checksum from FUN_00440038, +3 sequence-number byte, which the triple-send path ORs with 0x40 and then 0x80. The sequence counter at 0x00512F4C wraps 1..39, one short of the forty slots.
globals.basis: Net_SendCommand's writes, read in full. The 0x104 stride and the 40-slot bound are exact; the name 'packet' is the inference.
globals.promotion: Follow FUN_004B90FB, the send. If it hands the slot to a transport with a length of 0x104 or of the declared payload plus four, the reading is confirmed either way.

globals.name: g_moveOrderDest
globals.comment: Whatever NetCmd_WriteMoveOrder passes to Net_ResolveDest to make the packet's second field.
globals.basis: One call site. Nothing else traced reads it.

globals.name: g_hoverDamper
globals.comment: Set to 40 when a move selection begins and decremented once per Map_HoverUnitTarget call while positive. Never read anywhere else in the traced corpus.
globals.basis: Two sites, both writes. A counter nothing reads is exactly the shape a reader should distrust: 'damper' is a guess at intent, not a finding.
globals.promotion: Find a reader. If there is none, say so and drop the name - an unread counter deserves a number, not a noun.

globals.name: g_lordPersonality
globals.comment: Stride 0x50, three rows a lord. Siege_Prepare reads *(int*)(base + (lord*3 - 3) * 0x50) to choose the AI's siege-engine order.
globals.basis: The indexing arithmetic, and docs/armies.md section 4's [D] reading of the branch. The name comes from what the branch is used FOR, which is the weakest kind of evidence and is C3's shape.
globals.promotion: Read the table out of the file with tools/oracle/tables.ps1 and check the values against kingdom.md section 8.2's four personalities. Three rows a lord at 0x50 is a layout claim that can be falsified by the bytes alone.

globals.name: g_moveOriginX
globals.comment: The tile a movement flood-fill was seeded from. Move_ResetSelection writes it and its Y twin at 0x00504024, plus the flat index at 0x004F4070.
globals.basis: One writer, read in full. No reader traced.
globals.promotion: Find a reader - most likely Move_ExtractPath's terminator or the panel that prints a distance.

globals.name: g_garrisonPendingCounty
globals.comment: The county Army_Garrison stashes for Army_GarrisonConfirm, alongside the unit at 0x0055CD58. The address sits 8 bytes BELOW g_units (0x0052F0B0), so it is not part of any unit record.
globals.basis: Two sites, matched writer and reader. That is all.
globals.promotion: Check no third site writes it.

claims.subject: The raised county defence never gets a moveAllowance or a sprite because Army_Tick has not run on it yet
claims.comment: battle-during.sav slot 6 is a defence raised the same turn and carries moveAllowance 0 AND spriteFrame 0, while the two ordinary armies in the same save carry 15 and a correct sprite. Army_Tick writes both unconditionally at the top of every tick. So 'moveAllowance is 15 for an army' (docs/armies.md section 1.2) is a tick-maintained invariant, not an initial value, and a freshly created army is briefly outside it.
claims.basis: Three unit records in one fixture, plus Army_Tick read in full. Two of three agree and the third disagrees in exactly the way the explanation predicts.
claims.promotion: A fixture in which a defence survives into a following turn: it should then read 15. Nothing available today can produce one.

claims.subject: Unit +0x07 lags +0x1B by one walk phase
claims.comment: battle-during.sav slot 5 has facing 2, walkPhase 0 and spriteFrame 82, where Army_Tick's formula gives 0x48 + 3*((2+1)&7) + g_unitWalkFrames[0] = 81. The other two armies match exactly. Army_Tick writes +0x07 and then calls Unit_Step, which advances +0x1B - so the saved sprite is one phase behind the saved phase, and 82 - 81 = 1 is a value the table actually contains.
claims.basis: Three records; the discrepancy is exactly one walk-frame unit and the ordering in Army_Tick explains it. This is a reading that fits, which is why it is here and not in symbols.json.
claims.promotion: Read Unit_Step's +0x1B update and confirm it runs after the sprite write on the path that produced this record. If it does not, the formula or the table is wrong instead.

claims.subject: Map_Click's fifth industry rung, record 4 for castle graphics
claims.comment: Map_Click maps a clicked building's graphic to an industry record: below 4 -> 1, below 7 -> 3, below 10 -> 2, below 0x0D -> 0, and 0x15 or above -> 4. The first four rungs agree exactly with Unit_TrampleTile's ruin ladder and County_PlaceResourceSites' placement, a three-way agreement. The fifth has no counterpart in either, and docs/armies.md section 3.5 lists only records 0..3.
claims.basis: One function. The other two functions are silent about record 4 rather than contradicting it.
claims.promotion: Find a fifth industry record in the county layout, or a second reader of index 4. Silence from two functions is not evidence for it.

claims.subject: MoveOrder_ConfirmGarrison offers to split an army that will not fit
claims.comment: When the castle's remaining capacity is below the incoming army's men, the callback sends message 0xA6 with the unit, the county and a fourth value, and L2.eng group 166 carries 'Your army contains' / 'more troops can be stationed here.' / 'Do you want to split your army?' beside its 'Cannot garrison castle.' heading. Nothing in the knowledge base records an army-splitting mechanic.
claims.basis: The strings are certain. That message 0xA6 leads to a working split, rather than to a prompt whose yes-branch does something else, is not.
claims.promotion: Find message 0xA6's handler and read what its yes-branch does to the two unit records.

claims.subject: The tile at county +0x74/+0x75 carries terrain 0x14 when no castle is built and 0x15..0x19 for castle types 1..5
claims.comment: battle-before.sav: county 2 has castleType 1 and its +0x74/+0x75 tile has terrain 0x15; county 3 has castleType 0 and terrain 0x14. Unit_ReachCastleBuilding fires on 0x15..0x19, five values for five castle types, and County_FindCastleTile stamps 0x14 over a bare plot at load.
claims.basis: Two counties in one save, a five-wide range matching a five-wide castle-type ladder, and the load-time stamp. Two data points do not establish five rungs.
claims.promotion: A save with a type 2..5 castle, or the writer that changes the tile when a castle is completed - which would give the mapping from code rather than from two coincidences.

claims.subject: County_RaiseDefence's mode-1 auto-equip moves men ten at a time
claims.comment: The AI branch loops at most 50 times over the six weapon slots, moving 10 men from the realm's stock into each slot per pass and stopping when the remaining headcount drops below 10. So an AI county's defence is equipped in blocks of ten, round-robin by weapon type, and the last nine men are always peasants.
claims.basis: The loop read in full. Never observed - the fixture's only raised defence is a neutral county on the mode-2 path, whose ladder IS verified.
claims.promotion: A save with a defence raised in an AI-owned county. The signature is a troop count divisible by 10 in every equipped slot.

claims.subject: Giving a besieging army a move order is the only routine way to lift a siege
claims.comment: Siege_Break has three callers: Unit_OrderMove on a successful type-1 order, Siege_LaunchAssault refusing for want of engines, and the siege screen's own button. Siege_ValidateLink can also clear +0x199, but only when the garrison side of the link has already gone.
claims.basis: An exhaustive grep of the writes to +0x199 across the whole corpus, which is mechanical. What is inferred is that the set is complete in the sense that matters - the corpus is decompiled C and an indirect write through a struct pointer would not be found by that grep.
claims.promotion: Nothing cheap. Recorded so that a later reader knows the grep was by field name, not by address.
